body:
Background: trying out mini.completion and it does not play well with ansible-language-server.

Completions contain raw tabs (`\t`), accepting any completion causes raw tab to be added as-is to the document (instead of adjusted for indentation), breaking yaml format and causing new diagnostics.

Server Problems:
* server sends [completion responses](https://github.com/ansible/vscode-ansible/blob/main/packages/ansible-language-server/src/providers/completionProvider.ts#L645) of textedits with raw tabs (`\t`). Does not check that client can handle this correctly :) I think this happens to work for vscode because it behaves differently with indentation, e.g. uses `InsertTextMode=2`
* server doesn't indicate [snippet](https://github.com/ansible/vscode-ansible/blob/main/packages/ansible-language-server/src/providers/completionProvider.ts#L572) format of the textedit until 'resolve'. I could be wrong, but this seems really broken to me, but might be easy to get fixed.

Client Problem:
* imagine some of above were fixed: `mini` still doesn't expand textedits of snippet format unless they have variables or tabstops. This means snippets with `\t` but no variables or tabstops won't be expanded with correct indentation. This part also seems wrong to me?

Should the logic maybe be adjusted to also look for tabs? I checked that many friendly-snippets have `\t` in them. Did not check any other LSP servers, and it will not solve my issue with this language server on its own, but may improve compatibility in general.

[snippet-hack.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22930421/snippet-hack.patch)

comment_data.body:
I know there is already a lot of details in here, but there is something I am missing to fully understand the issue. Could you, please, provide a reproducible example of the issue you describe? It can be with `ansible-language-server` (in which case it requires exact file, cursor position, and sequence of key presses needed to repro). But I'd appreciate an example of an actual snippet body together with text and cursor position to where this snippet is trying to be inserted.

Quick test showed that I did not have issues with preserving indentation (although `\t` did insert literally and there were some other issues with matching). Here is what I just did to try to see:
- Create the '~/.config/nvim/snippets/global.json' file with the following contents:

    ```json
    {
      "Just text": {
        "prefix": "ctext",
        "body": "Just some\n\tMulti\n\tLine\nText",
        "description": "Multiline text"
      }
    }
    ```

- Use the following 'mini.snippets' setup:

    ```lua
    local snippets, config_path = require('mini.snippets'), vim.fn.stdpath('config')
    snippets.setup({
      snippets = {
        snippets.gen_loader.from_file(config_path .. '/snippets/global.json'),
      },
    })
    MiniSnippets.start_lsp_server()
    ```
- Start new Neovim session and in an empty buffer in Insert mode type `<Space><Space>abc<CR>` (this would, probably, preserve two space indentation on a new line; if not - make sure that it is there).
- Press `<C-Space>`. This shows the single available snippet from the 'mini.snippets' LSP server. Yes, it is not marked as snippet.
- Press `<C-n>` to select the entry. It makes it appear in the buffer.
- Press `<C-y>` to accept candidate. This result in the following buffer text (before `Multi` and `Line` there are literal `\t`, but they are indented):

    ```
      abc
      Just some
      	Multi
      	Line
      Text
    ```

> Server Problems:

Yes, both look like a server issues. Especially not providing insert kind before 'resolve'. This is against LSP specification and will not work in 'mini.completion'.

Yes, I'll give you a repro. It is confusing.

The basic problem is that yaml file is indented with spaces. The insertion of the raw `\t` causes language server to complain about "illegal tab character" (with associated diagnostics emitted), and it messes up subsequent completion until you manually change the tab to spaces. 

When response is marked as snippet, it is not expanded as literal `\t` but instead expanded as spaces.

reply_data.body: Here is example repro with a screenshot. if you name it `playbook.yml` and open it with ansible_ls you should be able to see it. ```yaml # Basic idea, create a new list element (like shown below) under "tasks": # # ``` # - name: test # asser # ``` # # After typing 'asser' you should have completion item of "ansible.builtin.assert" available. # after accepting completion you should have: # # - name: test # ansible.builtin.assert: # <-- cursor indented (NO TABS). if you type 't' it should then complete 'that:' ... and so on - name: Example hosts: localhost gather_facts: false tasks: - name: test ansible.builtin.assert: that: [ true ] ``` Maybe this screenshot also helps if you look closely at the `listchars`. You can see there is no issue with indentation, the problem is just the raw tab. It breaks the language-server's parsing: * causes it to not suggest "that:" as an option, even though it is mandatory * suggests other things instead that are invalid * issue diagnostic about malformed yaml The inserted `\t` also causes a treesitter parsing error and incorrect highlighting.

Here is example repro with a screenshot. if you name it playbook.yml and open it with ansible_ls you should be able to see it.

# Basic idea, create a new list element (like shown below) under "tasks":
#
# ```
# - name: test
#   asser
# ```
#
# After typing 'asser' you should have completion item of "ansible.builtin.assert" available.
# after accepting completion you should have:
#
# - name: test
#   ansible.builtin.assert:
#     <-- cursor indented (NO TABS). if you type 't' it should then complete 'that:' ... and so on
- name: Example
  hosts: localhost
  gather_facts: false
  tasks:
    - name: test
      ansible.builtin.assert:
        that: [ true ]

Maybe this screenshot also helps if you look closely at the listchars. You can see there is no issue with indentation, the problem is just the raw tab. It breaks the language-server's parsing:

  • causes it to not suggest "that:" as an option, even though it is mandatory
  • suggests other things instead that are invalid
  • issue diagnostic about malformed yaml

The inserted \t also causes a treesitter parsing error and incorrect highlighting.

> ... it would just still require a change on the mini side to ensure it is treated that way.

At first glance, I think it makes sense here to restrict number of cases when candidate is marked as snippet but 'mini.completion' does not treat it as such. I'd go even further and make the extra check not for tabstop, but for any whitespace (`word:find('%s') ~= nil`). If it is marked as a snippet and contains a whitespace, then it probably needs to be treated as a snippet.

It still seems to work for the use case that prompted this workaround solution (described in the comment; like LSP server marking *every* candidate as snippet, even just words).

reply_data.body:
I don't think "Many clients (e.g. neovim mini.completion) cannot defer the insertTextFormat property until completionItem/resolve:" is the best reason for this change.

There is a dedicated [`resolveSupport` field of client capabilities](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#completionClientCapabilities) which lists all the fields that client can handle supplied in `completionItem/resolve` response. All other properties that are not included in that list [*must* be provided in `textDocument/completion` response](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#textDocument_completion).

So if `insertTextFormat` is absent in `resolveSupport` property array, then it *must* be supplied in `textDocument/completion` response or never at all. Otherwise the server violates the LSP specification.
